# Generated files

This page lists the files `Generate` writes, when it refuses to write them, and the modules the generated code imports, for a developer wiring wiregen's output into a TypeScript build.

## What Generate writes

`Registry.Generate(ctx, opts...)` writes these files under `WithTSDir`, by the names the options set, plus the OpenAPI document at each path `WithOpenAPIFiles` names:

| File | Written when |
| --- | --- |
| `types.gen.ts` | always |
| `decoders.gen.ts` | always |
| `validators.gen.ts` | always |
| `events.gen.ts` | `Events` is non-empty |
| `constants.gen.ts` | `Constants` is non-empty |
| `client.gen.ts` | `Endpoints` is non-empty, see [Typed HTTP client](http-client.md) |
| the arbitraries module | `WithArbitrariesFile` is set, see [Property-test arbitraries](arbitraries.md) |
| the OpenAPI document | `WithOpenAPIFiles` is set, with the same bytes at every path it names |
| `deadset-edges.json` | `WithDeadsetEdges` is set, at the target root it names or at the path `WithDeadsetEdgesFile` names, see [Deadset edges file](#deadset-edges-file) |

Every TypeScript file starts with the header comment, `// Code generated by wiregen. DO NOT EDIT.` unless `WithHeaderComment` changes it. The output is byte-identical from run to run.

## Errors and writing

`Generate` builds every file in memory first, and returns an error and writes nothing when:

- the `Registry` or the context is nil, `WithTSDir` is missing, or `WithTransportImport` is missing while endpoints are registered.
- a type or enum is registered with no package or name, twice, or under a bare name another package's type also takes.
- two enums emit the same TypeScript type name or value-array name, or an enum cannot be resolved (see [Enums](type-mapping.md#enums)).
- a registered type is not a struct or a map, or a field cannot cross the wire with a checked shape (see [What Generate refuses](type-mapping.md#what-generate-refuses)).
- a union does not fit its type (see [Unions](type-mapping.md#unions)).
- an event has no name, a name with a line break, no data type, or a name used twice.
- two generated names collide in the modules' shared namespace (see [Identifiers](type-mapping.md#identifiers)).
- a TypeScript output is absolute or leaves the TS directory, by its path or through a symlink, or two outputs, TypeScript or OpenAPI, are one file: from some file or directory on both paths, compared by device and inode once its symlinks are followed, the same names below it, compared without case, whether or not the file exists yet.
- a `Const`'s `TSName` has no characters left once cleaned to an identifier.
- the endpoint table is invalid (see [Validation](http-client.md#validation)), names a security scheme `OpenAPI.SecuritySchemes` does not declare or lists an empty or repeated role, has a server with no URL, a server URL that is not valid UTF-8 or holds outside its placeholders a query, fragment, space, control character, double quote, any of `` <>\^`| `` or a `%` that starts no percent-encoding, a variable value holding one or a brace, a malformed or repeated placeholder, a `{name}` no variable defines, a variable its URL does not use, or a variable with no `Default` or a `Default` outside its `Enum`, or a scheme is malformed.
- a mapping has no `TS`.
- a `TSNameOverride`, `PathNameOverride` or `EnumTSNameOverride` key names no registered type or enum, or a `Mappings` key is reached by no registered type's field.
- OpenAPI files are named without `OpenAPI.Title` and `Version`, an OpenAPI path climbs with `..` out of a directory that does not exist, a mapping has no `Schema`, two components would share a name, or a `$ref` in the document is not a string or names nothing in it.
- `WithDeadsetEdgesFile` is set without `WithDeadsetEdges` or names a path whose last element is empty, `.` or `..`, the TS directory lies outside the edges file's directory, the `WithDeadsetEdges` target root gives the registered types and enums no edge, or the existing edges file is not a valid edges document or holds a hand-written edge under `wiregen/`, as [Deadset edges file](#deadset-edges-file) describes.
- the registered packages fail to load or type-check.

Every error that lists fields lists all of them, so one run reports every fix.

Each file, the OpenAPI documents included, is then staged with [filesafe](https://github.com/cplieger/go/tree/main/filesafe) as a temporary file beside its target, creating any missing parent directory as `os.MkdirAll` does, with the mode the umask leaves, and only once every file is staged is each committed: synced, renamed into place and its directory synced. A staging failure, such as a full disk, an unwritable directory or a target that is not a regular file, leaves every target untouched and no temporary file behind, though a parent directory it created stays. Each commit is atomic, but the commits run one after another, so a failure partway through them can leave some files new and others old.

`ctx` bounds the package load, which runs the `go` command as a subprocess. Cancelling it stops the pass, and the cancellation reason, including a cause set with `context.WithCancelCause`, is reachable with `errors.Is`.

## Validators module

The decoders import their checks by name from `validators.gen.ts`, which wiregen writes on every run, so it always matches the decoders and you never edit it. Your own hand-written decoders may import and build on the same helpers.

A failed check throws a `TypeError` whose message starts with the JSON path, such as `$.user.id: expected number, got string`. `decodeArray` and `decodeRecord` add the element index or key to the path. The module exports:

- `type Decoder<T> = (v: unknown) => T`
- `own(o: globalThis.Record<string, unknown>, key: string): unknown`, reading only an own property, so an inherited `constructor` or `toString` reads as `undefined`
- `asObject(v: unknown, path = "$"): globalThis.Record<string, unknown>`
- `asArray(v: unknown, path = "$"): unknown[]`
- `reqStr`, `reqNum` and `reqBool(o: globalThis.Record<string, unknown>, key: string, path = "$")`, where `reqNum` rejects `NaN` and `Infinity`
- `reqRaw(o, key, path = "$"): unknown`, which refuses an absent key and passes any present value, `null` included, through as data. The decoders read a required field through it when they take the value whole: a `json.RawMessage`, a struct, a type mapped with no `Decoder`, or a named map that reads `null` as `{}`. A named map that refuses `null` is read through `asObject` instead
- `optStr`, `optNum` and `optBool(o, key, path = "$")`, returning `undefined` for an absent key, for hand-written decoders
- `reqOneOf<T extends string>(o, key, vals: readonly T[], path = "$"): T`
- `decodeArray<T>(v: unknown, decode: Decoder<T>, path = "$"): T[]`
- `decodeRecord<T>(v: unknown, decode: Decoder<T>, path = "$"): globalThis.Record<string, T>`, whose every key, `__proto__` included, is an own property
- `refuseKeys(o, keys: readonly string[], path = "$"): void`, which refuses a present, non-null value at any of `keys`
- `checkRange(v: number, lo, hi, path = "$")`, `checkBytes(s: string, max, path = "$")`, `checkPattern(s: string, pattern, path = "$")` and `checkCount(a: T[], lo, hi, path = "$")`, each returning its value or throwing

## Events module

With `Events` registered, `events.gen.ts` exports:

- `type EventFrame`, the union of `{event: "<name>", data: <Type>}` over every event.
- `type EventName`, the union of the event names.
- `EVENT_DECODERS`, one decoder per event name.
- `decodeEventFrame(event: string, data: unknown): EventFrame`, which decodes one frame and throws on an unknown name.

Your event-stream code reads each `EventSource` message's `event` and parsed `data` and passes them to `decodeEventFrame`. No module of yours is imported.

## Deadset edges file

[deadset](https://github.com/cplieger/deadset) finds unused code across Go and TypeScript. A Go wire type that only the generated TypeScript reads looks unused to it. An [edges document](https://github.com/cplieger/deadset-spec/blob/dev/docs/edges.md) declares that use, and `WithDeadsetEdges(targetRoot)` writes one for everything wiregen generates.

Pass the directory deadset analyses, relative to the working directory. wiregen writes `deadset-edges.json` there, the one name and place deadset reads. The TS directory must lie below it. When a type or an enum is registered, at least one edge must come out, so a package declaring a paired symbol must have its files below the root. That is a registered type's or enum's package, or one declaring a struct a registered type embeds, directly or through another embed. A root giving none is refused with an error naming the root and the registered packages, since the file would hold no edge. A registry with no type or enum writes a file with no edges.

```go
err := r.Generate(ctx, wiregen.WithTSDir("web/src/wire"), wiregen.WithDeadsetEdges("."))
```

Each edge pairs a Go symbol with the TypeScript symbol generated from it.

| Go symbol | TypeScript symbol | Identifier |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a registered struct, named map or union | its type in the types file | `wiregen/<Type>` |
| a field of a registered struct | the property in the types file, by its wire name | `wiregen/<Type>/<Field>` |
| an embedded struct whose fields are flattened into a registered type | that type, since the embed has no property of its own | `wiregen/<Type>/<Embed>` |
| a field of a union that one case alone carries | the property in that case | `wiregen/<Type>/<Field>` |
| a field of a union that several cases carry, the tag among them | the union's type, since deadset names no property two cases declare | `wiregen/<Type>/<Field>` |
| an enum type | its type in the types file | `wiregen/<Enum>` |
| an enum constant, one repeating another's value included | the enum's value array in the decoders file, or the enum's type when no decoder reads the enum | `wiregen/<Enum>/<Const>` |

A field promoted from an embedded struct is paired as that struct's field, such as `Base.ID`, and its identifier keeps the dot, as in `wiregen/User/Base.ID`. The embed itself is paired as a field of the struct that declares it: `User.Base` for `User` embedding `Base`, and `Base.Meta` with the identifier `wiregen/User/Base.Meta` when `Base` embeds `Meta`. An embedded alias of a struct literal, `type Meta = struct { Rev int }`, declares its fields itself, so `Rev` is paired as `Meta.Rev`, while an alias of a named struct leaves its fields to that struct. Each Go name rune outside ASCII is written as `-u` and six hex digits in the identifier. A property is named bare when deadset spells it bare, else in single quotes, as in `User.'display name'`. A `Const` has no Go symbol, and endpoints and events are strings, so none of them gets an edge.

The TypeScript side names its package the way deadset does. wiregen walks up from the generated file to the edges file's directory, and the first `package.json` with a `name` gives `ts://<name>/<path below that package.json>`. With none, the side reads `ts://./<path below the edges file's directory>`. A byte the reference cannot hold there is percent-encoded with uppercase hex: in the package name, any byte other than an ASCII letter, a digit, `.`, `_` and `-`, keeping a scoped name's `@` and `/`; in the path, a control character (DEL included), a space, `#` and `%`. A directory named `my wire` is therefore `my%20wire`. A Go package whose files lie outside the target root gets no edges, because deadset cannot see it, as long as another package gives the file an edge.

Every generated edge has `"because": "generated by wiregen"`. When the file exists, wiregen keeps its `description` and the body of every edge outside `wiregen/` as written, escapes included, and replaces every edge under `wiregen/`. A removed type therefore loses its edges, and running again without changes writes the same bytes.

Generate refuses, naming each identifier, an edge under `wiregen/` without that `because`, so a hand-written edge is never deleted. Rename such an edge outside the prefix. Generate also refuses a file that is a symbolic link or not a regular file, such as a directory or a FIFO, is not JSON, holds a duplicate key or a member other than `description` and `edges`, or has a `description` that is neither a string nor null. A null `description` is dropped, and a null or missing `edges` reads as no edges. deadset itself checks the edges you wrote.

wiregen writes every edge its output needs, spelled as deadset-spec's reference grammar spells it, and does not hold the file to what a given deadset release accepts. A deadset release that predates the grammar's support for them refuses a side holding a quoted member with a space or a percent-encoded scope, and every release refuses a file larger than 1 MiB. wiregen reads back any file it wrote, whatever its size.

The file is written with the other outputs, edge identifiers and the members of wiregen's own edges sorted, a hand-written edge's members in the order written, two-space indents and a trailing newline. Commit it, and check in CI that regenerating leaves it unchanged, so a stale edge fails before deadset reports it.

### Writing into another tree

Only the Go packages whose files lie below the target root get edges, wherever wiregen generates. The TypeScript side is scoped from the output tree, the directory holding the edges file, which by default is the target root. `WithDeadsetEdgesFile(path)` moves the edges file, and with it the output tree: the TS directory must lie below the file's directory, the `package.json` walk stops there, and the existing file read for hand-written edges is the one at `path`.

Generating into another tree that holds the same `package.json` files, `description` and hand-written edges therefore writes what generating in place writes. So a CI check can regenerate into a temporary directory and compare the result with the committed files. The comparison must cover every committed generated file, `deadset-edges.json` included, so a file the temporary directory lacks fails the check, as `diff -r` does. Copy into it each `package.json` that lies between the edges file and the TS directory, since it names the TypeScript side's package.

Do not copy the committed edges file. Generate merges into the file at the path, so a copy already holds the committed generated edges, and the comparison still passes when the edges are no longer written. With no hand-written edges and wiregen's default `description`, copy nothing, so Generate writes the whole file. A missing edges write then leaves no edges file, which that comparison fails.

Otherwise, seed the temporary file with the committed file's `description` and its edges outside `wiregen/`. Generate replaces each `wiregen/` edge whose `because` is `"generated by wiregen"` and refuses any other. So in a committed file it accepted, dropping the `wiregen/` edges leaves exactly the hand-written ones. Keep their bytes as written, as `jsontext.PreserveRawStrings` does below, since Generate writes them back as read and the comparison is byte for byte.

```go
// tmp holds a copy of web/package.json; repoRoot is the directory deadset
// analyses. Skip seedHandEdges only when the committed file has no edge
// outside wiregen/ and wiregen's default description. An omitted
// description is not the default.
if err := seedHandEdges(filepath.Join(repoRoot, "deadset-edges.json"), filepath.Join(tmp, "deadset-edges.json")); err != nil {
    return err
}
err := r.Generate(ctx,
    wiregen.WithTSDir(filepath.Join(tmp, "web", "src", "wire")),
    wiregen.WithDeadsetEdges(repoRoot),
    wiregen.WithDeadsetEdgesFile(filepath.Join(tmp, "deadset-edges.json")))

// seedHandEdges writes the edges document at committed to seed without the
// edges under wiregen/. json is encoding/json/v2.
func seedHandEdges(committed, seed string) error {
    data, err := os.ReadFile(committed)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    var doc struct {
        Description jsontext.Value            `json:"description,omitzero"`
        Edges       map[string]jsontext.Value `json:"edges"`
    }
    if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &doc); err != nil {
        return err
    }
    maps.DeleteFunc(doc.Edges, func(id string, _ jsontext.Value) bool {
        return strings.HasPrefix(id, "wiregen/")
    })
    out, err := json.Marshal(doc, jsontext.PreserveRawStrings(true))
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }
    return os.WriteFile(seed, out, 0o644)
}
```

The path is relative to the working directory, and its directory is resolved as the operating system opens it. A path whose last element is empty, `.` or `..` names no file and is refused, and so is `WithDeadsetEdgesFile` without `WithDeadsetEdges`.
